title: Leading Vistra's Transformation Through Client Focus, Digital Innovation, and Operational Clarity
author: CFI.co Editorial
content_html:
Over the past year, Vistra’s leadership team has re-oriented Vistra around a single organising principle: the client comes first. Their three priorities, strengthening client focus through empowered market leaders, combining digital capability with AI to reshape the client experience, and simplifying the organisation to scale, are driving how the firm supports cross-border business expansion globally.

A Leadership Team Focused on Execution

[caption id="attachment_28917" align="alignright" width="300"] CEO: Kim Jenkins[/caption]

When Kim Jenkins became CEO of Vistra in mid-2025, the strategic vision was already established: to become a digitally powered professional services leader blending the power of digital with a deep global bench of industry expertise.  This direction has not changed. Instead, the focus on execution has been sharpened, and based on a diagnostic of the business, the operating structure has been sharpened, and Vistra is clear on a path that puts the client at the centre of every decision and strategic priority.

Jenkins describes the choice clearly. Companies must decide between three core strategic DNAs: client-first, operational excellence, or product leadership. All three matter, but one must have primacy. She chose 'client-first' as the primary strategic imperative for Vistra. Every investment in digital solutions, AI, process improvement, and new capabilities starts with a client need and exists to meet that need in the best possible way.

That clarity of purpose underpins the three priorities now shaping Vistra's transformation.

Priority One: Strengthening Client Focus Through a Market-led Model

The first priority is strengthening client focus through Vistra's market-led model.

Market leaders hold end-to-end responsibility for winning new business, managing client relationships, and service delivery within their jurisdictions. Bringing these responsibilities together has created clearer accountability and a more connected experience for clients. The logic is simple: for clients, there is only one relationship with Vistra.

Market leaders understand the regulations, culture, language, and commercial practices of their jurisdictions. They are closest to the client and have the authority to make decisions and deploy resources, while drawing on Vistra's global reach, specialist expertise, and common standards. The wider organisation, including global functions, centres of excellence, and specialist teams, is structured to support them.

For clients, the difference is felt directly. Decisions are made closer to where they operate. Questions are answered by people who understand local context. And accountability sits with a single leader rather than being diffused across functions.

Vistra’s leadership team places strong emphasis on continuous improvement within this model. Colleagues are expected to challenge assumptions, identify operational barriers, and share what they observe close to the client. Innovation flows in both directions: strategic priorities are set centrally, while market leaders surface client needs and operational insights that shape how the business evolves with overall responsibility for the entire client lifecycle – from sales to account management to service delivery.

Priority Two: Delivering a Seamless, Consistent Global Client Experience through Vistra Digital

The second priority brings together Vistra's digital capability and AI investment into one integrated ambition: reshaping how clients experience the business. Jenkins describes this as "Powered by digital, delivered by experts".

For businesses managing entities across multiple jurisdictions with increasing regulatory demands, Vistra Digital cuts through operational complexity. Clients have a single place to manage their entity estates, access and upload documents, monitor service requests, and communicate securely with Vistra experts. Anywhere, anytime. A client in an airport lounge who needs a document after hours in Hong Kong can log in, retrieve it, and carry on. Geni, Vistra's AI agent, helps clients retrieve information and track service requests, while those who prefer to pick up the phone or email their relationship manager can continue to do so.

The experience is designed around choice: some clients want extensive digital self-service with AI enablement, others prefer purely human interaction, and many move between the two depending on what they need. In corporate and fund services, where regulatory obligations vary between jurisdictions and complex decisions require professional judgement, that flexibility matters. Digital tools and capability improves access, speed, and transparency. Vistra's professionals provide the expertise and assurance that technology alone cannot.

Underpinning the client experience is a deliberate investment in AI capability and building AI literacy across the organisation. Jenkins has personally championed this, with senior leaders expected to understand AI's potential and model responsible adoption. All Vistra colleagues have access to Microsoft's CoPilot AI solution, and around 2,500 colleagues are active users of AWS Quick. Earlier this year, Vistra received the Microsoft AI Frontier Award for Reinventing Customer Engagement, recognising how AI is being embedded into operations and transforming client engagement.

Colleague-led innovation has generated over 100 team-sourced AI use cases addressing areas of friction and client need, now being developed on a prioritised basis. For Jenkins, the equation is clear. Technology without expertise creates risk. Expertise without technology creates inefficiency. Vistra's operating model is built to deliver both.

Priority Three: Simplifying the Organisation to Scale

The third priority is simplification: ensuring Vistra’s global scale translates into a consistent, responsive experience for clients.

With broad international reach and deep expertise across markets, Vistra can support clients wherever they operate. The focus now is on making that capability easier to access by strengthening accountability, simplifying ways of working and connecting expertise more effectively across the organisation.

For clients, this means clearer points of contact, more consistent experiences across markets, and faster access to the right expertise. It also supports a more seamless journey from onboarding through to ongoing service delivery.

Simplification also enables Vistra’s other priorities to deliver greater value. Connected digital tools and AI are most effective when they support clear processes and coordinated teams. A market-led model is strongest when local decision-making is backed by global capability without unnecessary barriers.

For colleagues, clearer accountability and more effective ways of working create more time to focus on clients and apply professional judgement where it matters most. The result is an organisation better able to combine global reach, local expertise and digital capability at scale.

Turning Strategy into Client Value

Each of these priorities, market-led accountability, digital and AI capability, and organisational simplification, is designed to deliver the same objective: making it easier for clients to operate and grow across borders.

That is Vistra's core territory. Businesses expanding internationally face regulatory complexity, jurisdictional risk, and operational fragmentation. Vistra de-risks expansion, handling what would otherwise slow them down so they can focus on what is strategically core to their business.

The recent acquisition of Biz Latin Hub extended Vistra's reach into a further 16 countries across Latin America. For clients, that scale provides a single trusted partner with local expertise, digital capability, and clear accountability wherever they enter a new market.

Jenkins is clear that scale only works if it doesn't come at the cost of responsiveness. It is why Vistra works hard to preserve the entrepreneurial energy and local knowledge that underpin its client relationships. Market leaders remain accountable in their jurisdictions. Global infrastructure supports local relationships.

That balance of reach with responsiveness, technology with expertise, global standards with local knowledge, is what Vistra is building. A transformation shaped by a consistent focus on what clients actually need.
